solution.summary: The bid delivers a hosted, cloud-based accounting and financial reporting platform for the City of Colfax, configured to replace the City's current Tyler Technologies Fund Balance modules (Accounts Payable with 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and approved purchase orders, Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing and Business Licensing) and implemented by a named project manager and technical team. Delivery runs in four phases that mirror the RFP's four tasks: discovery and project management planning, installation and implementation with five years of historical data imported, training and documentation, then twelve months of post-implementation support and ongoing annual services. The platform is procured as a subscription with implementation services, priced as a fixed total with a capped reimbursable allowance, and scheduled to go live by July 1, 2026. A governance and compliance workstream runs alongside delivery to carry the RFP's contractual, insurance, certification, offshoring-notice and communication obligations. The bid team is a single prime vendor accountable for all items, with any third-party applications disclosed and priced.

components.title: Project management, governance and weekly reporting
components.description: A dedicated project manager plus named technical staff run the engagement from award to go-live and through the support term, with a written personnel management plan identifying roles, hours of availability and escalation paths. The vendor holds weekly progress, budget and timeline meetings with the City's Accounting and IT staff, producing a status report, a budget-to-actual tracker and a refreshed schedule each week. The plan sequences work from contract award (targeted October 22, 2025) to the July 1, 2026 go-live, with a task-level timeline and dependencies, and it names the City staff whose time is needed at each stage so the City can plan around the fiscal year-end close. The vendor also confirms availability for a virtual finalist interview on September 25, 2025 if the City requires one.

claims.text: The City's stated goal is to go live on the new system by July 1, 2026, the start of its fiscal year, which leaves roughly nine months from the targeted October 22, 2025 award.

The City has 11 full-time employees (one position vacant) plus one part-time/seasonal/contract employee, so City-side project capacity is limited and the vendor must carry most of the delivery workload.

components.title: Hosted accounting and financial reporting platform
components.description: The vendor supplies a cloud-hosted accounting and financial reporting system covering the City's full current functional footprint: Accounts Payable including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and purchase orders with approval routing; Accounts Receivable; General Ledger; Payroll; Utility Billing; and Business Licensing. Transactions post systematically through configurable approval workflows, and the budgeting and forecasting module supports multi-year projections, budget-to-actual comparison and scenario modelling against the City's $6 million revenue base and June 30 fiscal year. Reporting and analysis tools include an ad hoc report writer, dashboards and export to spreadsheet for council and management reporting, and the system retains a full transaction and change audit trail with document attachment so records remain auditable and retrievable for future reference. The response identifies the license types offered at each level of use, describes how account numbers can be structured and customized, and states where any additional application or third-party vendor is used to meet a requirement rather than presenting it as native functionality.

claims.text: The City currently runs Tyler Technologies Fund Balance with Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing and Business Licensing modules used by five users.
The City operates on a $6 million annual budgeted revenue base and its fiscal year ends June 30.

components.title: Implementation, account structure and data migration
components.description: Implementation is delivered as a structured build-and-configure engagement: the vendor installs and configures the hosted environment, works with the City's auditors' expectations and the City's reporting requirements to recommend an account structure that supports auditable reporting, and assists Accounting staff in writing the financial reports the City needs for council, audit and grant purposes. The vendor imports the prior five years of historical data from the City's existing system, with reconciliation and control totals signed off by Accounting before cutover. Cutover is planned around the June 30 fiscal year-end so that the prior-year close completes in the legacy system and the new system opens the fiscal year 2026-27 books, with parallel running and a documented rollback point to minimize downtime and operational disruption. The vendor coordinates directly with the City's Accounting and IT contacts on network, identity and data-extract dependencies, and the implementation completes by July 1, 2026.

claims.text: The City's current system is Tyler Technologies Fund Balance, which is the source system for the five years of historical data to be imported.
The City's fiscal year ends June 30, so the July 1, 2026 go-live coincides with the opening of a new fiscal year.

components.title: Training, documentation and change management
components.description: The vendor delivers personalized, role-based training and written manuals for the City's power users in Accounting, covering configuration, period close, report writing and troubleshooting, so the City can maintain the system without vendor dependence. All remaining staff receive at least one recorded training session plus a written manual, and the recordings and manuals are handed over as City property for onboarding future employees. Training is delivered in the format appropriate to each license level and the response states whether each session is in person, virtual or a standard recording. Because the City has a small staff with one vacant position, training is scheduled in short sessions outside close periods and each session is recorded so staff can revisit it.

claims.text: The City has 11 full-time employees with one position vacant plus one part-time/seasonal/contract employee, so training must be repeatable and self-service for a small team.

components.title: Ongoing support, help desk and annual services
components.description: The vendor provides dedicated technical support during implementation and for the first twelve months after go-live, and continues that support through each annual contract renewal. Support is delivered through a help desk and ticketing system with defined priority levels, response and resolution targets, published hours of coverage and named escalation contacts, so the City can see how a request is prioritized and tracked. The vendor pushes automated software updates and issues advance communications describing changes, including release notes and any action required by the City. The vendor supports the City's annual e-filing obligations, including 1099 and W-2 preparation and submission, and provides an account manager as the City's single point of contact for recurring services. The response describes the support levels offered both during implementation and for recurring licenses and services, and outlines virtual demonstrations of product capabilities available to the City.

claims.text: The City's current Accounts Payable module includes 1099 filing, and the City wants dedicated technical support during implementation and throughout annual contract renewals.

components.title: Audit-readiness and reporting assurance
components.description: The vendor assigns a solution architect with local government audit experience to document how the configured system satisfies the City's auditing and reporting requirements, including segregation of duties, approval evidence, journal entry controls and retention of supporting documentation. This produces an audit-readiness pack the City can hand to its external auditors, mapping each control to where it is enforced in the system, and a recommended chart-of-accounts structure that keeps fund, function and object dimensions reportable without rework. The pack is reviewed with Accounting before go-live and refreshed after the first post-implementation audit cycle.

claims.text: The City needs to maintain auditable records and documentation for future reference and requires the vendor to understand its auditing and reporting requirements.

components.title: Price proposal and cost transparency
components.description: The vendor submits a complete price proposal on the City's Attachment A cover sheet stating a total price for all services and deliverables, a total reimbursable expenses cap, and a total price proposal amount, with the arithmetic between the three figures shown explicitly. The price is all-inclusive of materials, supplies and travel, and is broken out into implementation fees and recurring fees, with license fees shown separately by license type and support fees split between implementation-period and post-implementation costs. The proposal also estimates the cost of any additional applications or third-party vendors identified in the solution, so the City can compare the total cost of ownership rather than a headline figure. Reimbursable expenses are capped at a stated ceiling with no unlimited reimbursement, and the vendor confirms that the price proposal is final and will not be altered during any clarification stage.

claims.text: The City will not accept unlimited reimbursable expenses and requires the price proposal to cap them.

components.title: Contract, compliance and certification obligations
components.description: The vendor accepts the RFP's terms as binding contract conditions, treats every "shall", "must" and "requirement" as a contractual obligation, and does not alter or delete the paragraph giving notice of the City's terms and conditions, since doing so is grounds for rejection as nonresponsive. The vendor observes the prohibition on communications with City staff, evaluation committee members and other parties about its own or competitors' proposals from submission until award, and accepts disqualification as the consequence of a violation. The vendor bears all costs of preparing and submitting its proposal and of participating in interviews, with no reimbursement from the City. The vendor signs the Certification of Financial Condition and notifies the City of any occurrence or condition that materially alters the truth of a statement in that certification within thirty days of the change. The vendor states whether any work will be performed outside the United States and, if so, lists those locations and describes the corporate structure, and gives the City written notice if it, its employees, subcontractors or other personnel relocate to locations outside the United States. The vendor also supplies proof of workers compensation and commercial general liability insurance and documentation of the measures protecting financial data and the secure access controls implemented.

claims.text: The City rejects additional or modified terms and conditions submitted with a proposal and treats any attempt to alter the notice paragraph as grounds for rejection.
The City will evaluate offshoring disclosures for additional risks and costs before award.

assumptions.text: The new system is assumed to be licensed for the City's current five named users plus headroom for the vacant position and seasonal staff, with additional licenses priced per user, since the RFP does not state a required user count.

Migration of the prior five years of history is assumed to come from the City's Tyler Technologies Fund Balance system, with the City supplying extracts and the vendor performing the import and reconciliation.
The July 1, 2026 go-live is treated as a firm contractual milestone with a documented contingency plan, not an aspiration, because the City ties it to the start of its fiscal year.

The twelve-month post-implementation support term is assumed to include remote help desk coverage during business hours with defined response targets, on-site visits priced separately as capped reimbursable travel, since the RFP does not define service levels.

The vendor proposes its own three-tier license and support structure (named user, concurrent user and read-only inquiry) and its own service levels, since the RFP does not define license or support tiers.
The reimbursable expenses cap is set by the vendor as a stated dollar ceiling covering travel and third-party costs, since the City prescribes no cap amount.

The total price proposal is presented as the sum of the total price for services and deliverables plus the reimbursable expenses cap, with all three figures shown so the City can verify the arithmetic.

Material changes to the Certification of Financial Condition are notified to the Contract Lead within 15 days in writing, with a copy to the City's accounting contact, resolving the conflict between the 15-day and 30-day periods in favour of the shorter one.

The Attachment F and Attachment G software requirements are assumed to match the functional scope described in the RFP's scope of work, and the vendor will complete both spreadsheets against that scope and flag any requirement it cannot meet natively.

The City's standard contract and General Contract Terms and Conditions are assumed to be its standard software and services terms, which the vendor will review before the July 31, 2025 question deadline and raise any exception as a question rather than in the proposal.

Insurance is assumed to be provided at limits of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate for commercial general liability plus statutory workers compensation, with the City named as additional insured, pending the City's stated limits.
Attachment G documentation is assumed to be satisfied by a SOC 2 Type II report, a written security and access-control narrative, and a completed security questionnaire.
The proposal is submitted both as one signed hard copy and as an emailed digital copy by the August 28, 2025 4:00 PM PST deadline, treating both methods as required rather than alternatives.
The implementation start is assumed to be triggered by contract award on or about October 22, 2025, with work beginning within two weeks of award and negotiation.
